text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima is at odds with his vice-chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel of the People's Party over the possibility of combining NATO membership with neutrality. Klima says the two are mutually exclusive.

- Experts see a 12 billion schillings gap in this year's budget. Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger says the government will meet its 68 billion schillings deficit target by saving in areas where no fresh legislation is required.
- The new Creditanstalt board will be presented on April 11, a day after the bank's share holder meeting.
- The pay differential in Austrian industry is growing. Workers in the oil sector earn for times as much as workers in the clothing sector.
- The Council of Ministers has finally approved a proposal governing new trade regulations. Many parts of industry are unhappy, arguing that farmers have emerged from the deal as the big winners.
- The government plans to save five to six billion schillings in non-essential expenditure in order to reach its budget deficit goal this year.
- Grants for new technology will be topped up to 6.2 billion schillings plus a "special budget" of one billion schillings, creating thousands of new jobs.
- Austria's trade deficit jumped 25.6 percent to 82 billion schillings in the first nine months of 1996.
- Economic researchers are sceptical that the government's budget will hold this year. Finance Minister Edlinger is confident of reaching the Maastricht criteria.
- Austrian banks have cut interest rates on savings due to low credit demand and a glut of money. However borrowing rates have been kept stable.
- The European Union says Austrian wine farmers' should no longer be excluded from tax on alcohol sales.
- U.S. fast food chains plan to double the number of restaurants in Austria over the next three years.
